issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) on SealSaloon, but the solution implements a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int) instead. This name/signature mismatch means students following the problem or using the provided Main (which calls acceptSupplyDelivery) would not find the expected method in the reference implementation, causing confusion and preventing straightforward cross-checking.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the problem and template by renaming the solution method receiveDelivery to acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) (keeping it static), or add a static acceptSupplyDelivery wrapper that delegates to receiveDelivery. Also ensure any sample usages (e.g., Main) and documentation use the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) to receive ingredient deliveries, and the template's Main also calls acceptSupplyDelivery. The solution implementation, however, provides a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int) instead. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual operation (accepting a supply delivery) creates confusion for students mapping the requirement to the implementation and will break expectation-based references in the template/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method receiveDelivery to acceptSupplyDelivery with the same signature (acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)), or add a new static acceptSupplyDelivery method that delegates to receiveDelivery, so the implementation matches the problem statement and template usage.
